title: The Lion Makers
text:
In a town there lived four young brahmins who were close friends. Three of them had studied for years and mastered many learned sciences, but they had little common sense. The fourth had no great learning, but he had plenty of sense. They decided to travel together to seek their fortune with their knowledge.

On the road through a forest they came upon the bones of a dead lion. The three scholars saw a chance to show what they could do. The first said he could put the bones back together into a skeleton. The second said he could cover it with skin, flesh and blood. The third said he could give it life.

The fourth friend begged them to stop. If they brought a lion to life, he said, it would kill them all. They scorned him as an ignorant man. So he asked them to wait a moment, and climbed a tall tree.

The first scholar assembled the skeleton. The second gave it flesh and skin. The third breathed life into it. The lion rose, saw three men standing in front of it, and killed them. When it had gone, the man with common sense climbed down from the tree and went home alone.
lesson: Technical skill tells you what you can do; judgment tells you whether you should. Listen to the person asking what happens next, even if they know less than you.
